messages:
incident-bot: PAGED oncall — PROD-east-1 GPU queue spiking. Queue length: ~12.3k pending tokens. Autoscaler reported repeated failures to create GPU nodes. Severity: P1. See logs: `autoscaler/controller` errors: 'UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRole' and 'Failed to apply taints'. Please ack and triage.

alex (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Starting checklist: confirm exact ASG/launch template, check IAM passrole, check node taint hook.

maya (infra): looking. cluster: prod-gpu-01, nodegroup: gpu-ng-east-1a-b. LaunchTemplate: lt-gpu-prod-2026. IAM role attached to LT seems to be `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/old-gpu-launch-role` — that role was rotated last week. Suspect PassRole policy missing.

chris (eng-sre): fwiw autoscaler logs show repeated 403 from EC2 API when trying to AttachRole to instance profile. snippet from CA logs: 
```
I020 22:34:01.123456 1 provisioning.go:201] Error launching instance: UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRole is not allowed for iamRole
\tstatus code: 403, request id: c3f4-...
```

sam (runtime): also seeing taint application failing during bootstrapping: kubelet tries to apply taint but kubelet-token can't update nodes because bootstrap role not in `NodeInstanceRole` map. Example from instance bootstrap output: 
```
Applying taint: runtime.gpu=reserved:NoSchedule -> kubelet error: permission denied updating node object
```

alex (oncall): initial customer impact: several infra-critical jobs queued (realtime inference requests) causing throttling to hosted API customers in prod-east region. CS pinged. Jordan, can you coordinate customer comms?

jordan (cust-succ): on it. Starting initial outage note: "We are seeing increased latency and request throttling in the East region due to GPU capacity issues. Engineering is actively mitigating. Will update in 30m."

maya (infra): quick mitigation options: 1) fix PassRole on launch template role/policy; 2) temporarily remove taint via user-data script (not ideal); 3) manually scale a CPU fallback pool and route low-priority jobs there; 4) manually provision instances with correct instance profile. Which do we want first?

alex (oncall): prefer 1 + 3. Fix IAM then create CPU fallback to reduce queue. If IAM fix takes >10m, we'll manually spin up nodes.

chris (eng-sre): I'm patching the IAM policy now. Running `aws iam put-role-policy --role-name gpu-launch-role --policy-document file://allow-passrole.json` with payload to allow `iam:PassRole` to the instance profile. Will post diff when done.

devops-bot: deploy started: iam/policies/allow-gpu-passrole.json -> prod (initiated by chris). CI run id: 84271

sam (runtime): prepping a CPU fallback - scaling manifest for `inference-cpu-fallback` with nodeSelector to cpu-pool. If we route lower-priority inference there, we can reduce immediate GPU pressure. Pushing manifest now.

alex (oncall): go ahead sam. Also, how long until the autoscaler will retry? CA backoff window currently 5m. After we fix IAM it should pick up pending nodes.

chris (eng-sre): IAM policy applied. Confirmed role now has PassRole for `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/InstanceProfileForGPU`. Pushing to LT: `aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-id lt-0abcd --version-description fix-passrole --launch-template-data file://lt-patch.json`.

incident-bot: Note: autoscaler will respect launch template changes on next scale attempt. Manual ASG update may be required to avoid backoff.

maya (infra): manually triggered ASG launch with corrected LT version for nodegroup gpu-ng-east-1a-b. Kicking off an instance. Instance i-0d9ef created. Boot logs attached below.

sam (runtime): saw instance join the cluster but taint application still failing initially — kubelet attempting before node-label controller ready. I'm re-running bootstrap script with `kubectl taint nodes i-0d9ef runtime.gpu=reserved:NoSchedule-` after node becomes Ready.

alex (oncall): good. Any sign of queue decreasing? Metrics?

chris (eng-sre): queue size dropping slowly — from 12.3k -> 7.9k after CPU fallback and 3 new nodes coming online. Waiting for autoscaler to stabilize.

jordan (cust-succ): updating customers: "We've reduced throttling by routing lower-priority requests to a CPU fallback and adding temporary capacity. Engineering estimates 60% of affected requests restored while full GPU capacity is recovered."

maya (infra): patched node bootstrap role mapping so kubelet can apply taints. Confirmed `kubectl get nodes` shows new nodes with taint `runtime.gpu=reserved:NoSchedule`.

chris (eng-sre): autoscaler resumed normal ops and started further scale-ups; no more 403s in logs. Will monitor for 15m.

alex (oncall): handed off to Maya for next 2h watchdog — will circulate post-incident summary once stabilized. Key actions: patched IAM passrole, updated launch template, manually launched node, applied taint fix in bootstrap, created CPU fallback. Customer impact minimized but not fully removed until all queued requests drain. If anyone sees a regression ping @alex and re-escalate.

maya (infra): acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if queue grows or new 403s appear.

chris (eng-sre): postmortem notes start here: suspected cause — deployment last week swapped `lt-gpu-prod-2026` to use `old-gpu-launch-role` missing PassRole for new instance profile. Need a guard in CI to validate LT->role policy consistency.

jordan (cust-succ): final customer note drafted and waiting for alex sign-off.

alex (oncall): signed. closing active paging. I'll drop a short retrospective template in #postmortems and include command diffs, timestamps, and remediation steps. Thanks team :thumbsup:
